clue.text: Footwear the couple on an icy footpath needed?

blocks.clueFragment: Footwear the couple on an icy footpath needed?
blocks.note: surface reading: a pair of people on a frozen path needed proper shoes or boots

blocks.clueFragment: the couple on an icy footpath
blocks.note: setter's reading: two people losing their footing on ice are a twosome who keep sliding

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is soft indoor footwear, but read the other way it describes two people (a pair) who are slipping on the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippers are soft indoor shoes, and they are always sold and worn as a matched couple.

clue.text: Fruit bun I agree needs cooking

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so the preceding words are mixed up into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A baker agrees that the bun still has to go in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: Aubergine is the British word for eggplant; botanically it is a berry, so a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the eggplant is a berry, the seed-bearing part of the plant, though cooks treat it as a vegetable.

clue.text: Commanded communist to go around mid-July

indicators.note: mid asks for the central letters of the month name that follows it
going around something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a red is a communist
the two central letters of the month

explanation.surface: A communist official is told to travel around in the middle of summer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule is to govern or give orders, so a ruler who ruled has commanded.

clue.text: Distance I've motored, Initially in queues

indicators.note: initially points to only the opening letter of the word just before it
in places the earlier pieces inside the word that follows

blocks.note: files are lines of people, one behind another
taken as written, without the apostrophe
opening letter of motored

explanation.surface: A driver complains of covering a long way stuck in traffic jams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' governs only the word just before it, so motored contributes one letter; the queues are lines, not traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured length of road, five times the imperial unit, is a distance someone might travel.

clue.text: Labour leader said you can find missing Lord

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
said means we use the sound of the next word, written as a letter

blocks.note: first letter of Labour
the letter U is pronounced like this pronoun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party chief claims you can track down a vanished peer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Lucan, a British earl, disappeared in 1974 after his children's nanny was murdered and has never been found.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh Earl of that title vanished in 1974 and was declared dead decades later, never located.

clue.text: A trip arranged by shrewd bishop

indicators.note: arranged means set out afresh, so the letters before it are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
arch means knowing or cunning

explanation.surface: A clever churchman has organised an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Orthodox churches a patriarch is a senior bishop presiding over a major see.

clue.text: Climbing in before party, eat away

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word reads from bottom to top
in tells us one piece sits inside the next

blocks.note: ere is an old word for before
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Guests going upstairs before a party are told to eat up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'Climbing in', but the parse takes 'party climbing' as one step and 'in before' as the next.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear something down gradually, as water or acid gnaws at rock or metal.

clue.text: Postpone upsetting us while away

indicators.note: upsetting means tipping over, so in a down clue the short word is turned upside down

blocks.note: taken as written
to while away time is to spend it idly

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a delay because the plan annoys us while we are on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend a meeting or sentence is to defer it or put it on hold until later.

clue.text: Bought off black bride, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one version among several, so the letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bride in a black dress might have been paid to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Bribing means paying someone illicitly to secure their cooperation, the same as buying them off.

clue.text: Where Belgium holds revolt

indicators.note: holds says the words before it contain the answer inside them

blocks.note: letters running across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about which country is in rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to rebel is to rise up against authority, which is what revolting means.

clue.text: Five court cases about middle-class holidays

indicators.note: middle asks for the central letter of the word joined to it
about means surrounding, so one word wraps around a piece

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
lawsuits are legal actions
the central letter of class

explanation.surface: Five lawsuits concerning middle-class families going on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacations are periods of rest away from work or study, the American word for holidays.

clue.text: Monotony of drill work on motorway

blocks.note: to drill a hole is to bore it
to do is to work or perform
M is the prefix of British motorway numbers, as in M1

explanation.surface: The tedium of roadworks drilling away on a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious sameness produces weariness and lack of interest, which is the state of being bored.

clue.text: Simplicity of a net I've designed

indicators.note: designed means newly drawn up, so these letters are laid out in fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone admires the plain style of a net they have made.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocent lack of sophistication or guile, an artless simpleness of mind.

clue.text: Doctor sick of exercise

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A doctor who is tired of working out.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a repeated training routine, such as a military or fire practice.

clue.text: Learner takes one timid person home in car

indicators.note: in asks for the word just before it to be placed inside the preceding piece

blocks.note: L is the learner driver's plate
I is the Roman numeral for one
a mouse is a shy, timid person
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A learner driver gives a shy passenger a lift home.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'in' is being at home, and the word 'in' after it then places that piece inside the timid person.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large luxurious chauffeured motor vehicle, a grand type of car.

clue.text: Free student I scolded

blocks.note: L for learner, a student
taken as written
berated means told off angrily

explanation.surface: A released student recalls a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberated means set loose from confinement or control, so free is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Be taking on a role as Napoleon

indicators.note: taking means absorbing, so the short word holds the pieces that follow

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: An actor is told to play the French emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was the French emperor, whose family surname this is.

clue.text: Count her fancy northern club

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or imagined, so the preceding words are dressed up in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Someone is told to include a woman in a tally for a smart club up north.
explanation.walkthrough: A truncheon is a British police baton.
explanation.definitionFit: A police baton is a short heavy stick, the kind of weapon called a club.

clue.text: Working on farm see fraternity member

indicators.note: working means being processed or reworked, so these letters are put into new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone labouring on a farm spots a member of a brotherhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons belong to a secretive fraternal order, a brotherhood with lodges and rituals.

clue.text: Airmen backing artist on leave wanted medley

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the Royal Air Force
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Pilots supporting a painter who is on leave were after a mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused jumble or hotchpotch, a mixture of assorted things.

clue.text: Company's Head Office exercise

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for head
O is the abbreviation for office
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: A firm's headquarters holds a training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head Office' looks like one phrase but splits into two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A house is a business firm or institution, as in a publishing or fashion house.

clue.text: Test a terrible container for one's property

indicators.note: the preceding words act as a box holding the answer within their letters

blocks.note: letters running across the three words, starting after the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone tries out a dreadful box for keeping belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test a terrible' reads like an anagram with 'terrible' as its signal, but there are only five letters to shuffle; the words instead hold the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is the land and possessions a person owns, everything they have taken together.

clue.text: Put off introducing infrequent transport

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of place, so the word before it is jumbled
introducing means bringing into, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: rare means seldom happening
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is discouraged by bringing in a bus service that seldom runs.
explanation.walkthrough: Transport here is the noun meaning overwhelming emotion, as in 'transports of joy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapture is intense delight or ecstasy, an emotional state also called transport.

clue.text: Little singer has raised gratuity 1p!

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, so in a down clue the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a tip is a gratuity
the digit one written as the Roman numeral
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small-time singer gets a tip of just one penny.
explanation.walkthrough: TIP, I and P together are turned upward. In Britain 1p is a one-penny coin; here it splits into I and P.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipit is a small songbird, so a little creature that sings.

clue.text: Best French sleeping accommodation in Central Greece

indicators.note: central means only the letters at the heart of the country name are wanted
in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: the two central letters of the country
lit is French for bed

explanation.surface: Top-quality French hotel rooms are found in the middle of Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the select top group, the best people of any set.

clue.text: Staff caught volunteers returning smelly animal

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word before it is read right to left

blocks.note: a pole is a staff
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the Territorial Army, Britain's former volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Workers caught volunteers coming back with a stinking creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a weasel-like mammal known for the foul-smelling fluid it releases.

clue.text: Lead from the local timber supplier

blocks.note: the, as a local in France would say it
the ash tree supplies hardwood

explanation.surface: A tip-off comes from the neighbourhood wood merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' is the dog's lead, not a clue or a tip; 'the local' asks for 'the' in the local language, French.
explanation.definitionFit: A leash is the strap or cord used to hold a dog, which the British call its lead.

clue.text: Aim to pilfer novel sound device

indicators.note: novel means new, so the preceding letters take a new form

blocks.note: taken as written, leaving out the small joining word

explanation.surface: A thief sets out to steal a new piece of audio equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link inside the fodder phrase and supplies no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An amplifier boosts electrical signals to drive loudspeakers, a piece of audio equipment.

clue.text: Turn away a vicar, coming back on time

indicators.note: coming back means travelling in reverse, so the word reads right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
Rev, short for Reverend, a vicar's title
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A clergyman returning punctually is sent off.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert your eyes is to turn them aside, so the two phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Being about ten to hope Helen's getting in touch?

indicators.note: being about suggests things moved around, so the letters are scattered and reset

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: At about ten to the hour, someone hopes that Helen will make contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Contacting somebody by phone call means being on a line with them, so it is one way of keeping in touch.
